title.en: Cain and Abel: The First Murder
title.zh: 該隱與亞伯：第一樁兇案

region.en: Land of Nod, east of Eden (symbolic pin for the wanderer's land)
region.zh: 挪得之地（伊甸以東流浪者之地的象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The two sons of Adam and Eve bring offerings; God accepts the shepherd's and rejects the farmer's, and Cain kills his brother in the field. Marked by God so none may kill him, the first murderer becomes a wandering founder.
summary.zh: 亞當夏娃二子獻祭，神悅牧者之祭而拒農者之祭；該隱在田間殺弟。神為其立記號，免人殺之；首殺者遂為流浪而建城者。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; Tetragrammaton rendered 'the LORD'; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Cain knew Abel his brother, and Cain said unto him, 'There is no justice, and there is no Judge, and there is no world to come, and there is no reward for the righteous and punishment for the wicked.' And they strove in the field, and Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.
passages.note: This passage blends a rabbinic aggadic expansion (Genesis Rabbah 22) with the biblical notice of Genesis 4:8; paraphrase of both, not verbatim.

passages.text: And the LORD said unto Cain: 'Where is Abel thy brother?' And he said: 'I know not; am I my brother's keeper?' And He said: 'What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto Me from the ground. And now, cursed art thou from the ground, which hath opened her mouth to receive thy brother's blood from thy hand.'

Cain feared that whoever found him would kill him, but God set a mark upon him, that no one should slay him, and he went out from the presence of the LORD and dwelt in the land of Nod, east of Eden. There he built a city and named it after his son. The field had drunk the first blood of human history, and the wandering of the murderer became the founding of the first city. Paraphrase of Genesis 4:12-17 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Lamech's Boast and the First Crafts

region.zh: 挪得之地（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Cain's line founds cities, tents, herds, metallurgy, and music — and escalates vengeance. Lamech sings the first recorded boast-song: 'I have slain a man for wounding me... if Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy and sevenfold.'
summary.zh: 該隱後裔建城、張幕牧畜、鍛造銅鐵、彈琴吹簫；而復仇升級。拉麥唱出首見之誇耀之歌：「傷我者我殺之……該隱遭報七倍，拉麥必遭報七十七倍。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Adah bare Jabal: he was the father of such as dwell in tents and have cattle. And his brother's name was Jubal: he was the father of all such as handle the harp and pipe. And Zillah, she also bare Tubal-cain, the forger of every cutting instrument of brass and iron.

Lamech called to his two wives and boasted of his vengeance: he had killed a young man for a wound and would repay injuries seventy-sevenfold — violence multiplying itself down Cain's line. In the same breath, the chapter invents civilization: cities, nomadism, music, and metallurgy all descend from the murderer's family. Paraphrase of Genesis 4:23-24 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Enoch Walked with God, and Was Not

region.en: Judean hills (symbolic pin for the silent taking)
region.zh: 猶大山地（無言被取之地的象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: In the death-lists of Genesis 5 one man breaks the pattern: Enoch, father of Methuselah, 'walked with God' and was taken without dying — the Bible's first ascension, seeded for the vast apocalyptic books later written under his name.
summary.zh: 創世記五章的死亡譜系中，唯有一人破例：以諾，瑪土撒拉之父，「與神同行」，未死而被取——聖經首次升天，為後世以其名所寫之啟示文學埋下根苗。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah. And Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters. And all the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty and five years. And Enoch walked with God, and he was not; for God took him.

title.en: Noah's Vineyard and the Curse of Canaan
title.zh: 挪亞葡萄園與迦南受咒

region.en: Ararat foothills (symbolic pin; landing region of the ark)
region.zh: 亞拉臘山麓（方舟停靠區之象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The world's first vineyard yields the world's first drunkard: Noah lies uncovered in his tent, Ham sees his father's nakedness, and for the act (or its mockery) Noah curses Ham's son Canaan to servitude — the etiological frame the Torah gives for Israel's later relations with the Canaanites.
summary.zh: 世上首座葡萄園造出首位醉者：挪亞赤身臥於帳中，含見父之裸；因所行（或所譏）挪亞咒其子迦南為僕——此為色列後與迦南人關係之釋義框架。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition. The 'curse of Ham' has been misused historically to justify slavery; the record notes the text curses Canaan, not Ham's whole descent, and describes the verse without endorsing later interpretations.

passages.text: And Noah began to be a husbandman, and he planted a vineyard. And he drank of the wine, and was drunken; and he was uncovered within his tent. And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brethren without.

Shem and Japheth walked backward with a garment on their shoulders and covered their father without seeing him. Waking, Noah learned what Ham had done and pronounced the curse not on Ham himself but on Ham's youngest son: 'Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren.' The passage ends by naming Noah's death at nine hundred and fifty years. Paraphrase of Genesis 9:23-29 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The Tower of Babel and the Confusion of Tongues

region.zh: 示拿地巴比倫（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: All earth speaks one language and builds a city and a tower 'with its top in heaven, lest we be scattered'. God comes down to look, confuses their language, and scatters them over the earth — the etiological myth of linguistic diversity, aimed at Mesopotamia's ziggurat culture.
summary.zh: 全地同一言語，同建城與塔，「塔頂通天，免得分散」。神降下觀看，變亂其口音，使其分散遍地——語言分歧之釋義神話，鋒芒直指美索不達米亞塔廟文化。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And they said: 'Go to, let us build us a city, and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven, and let us make us a name; lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth.' And the LORD came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of men builded.

The LORD saw that one people with one language could accomplish anything they planned, so He confounded their speech so that no one understood another, halted the building, and scattered them across the earth. The city's name — Babel — is heard as Hebrew 'balal', 'He confounded', punning on the great city Babylon. Paraphrase of Genesis 11:6-9 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Lech Lecha: Abraham's Call to Go

region.en: Haran to Shechem (route pin at Haran)
region.zh: 自哈蘭至示劍（以哈蘭為路線定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: God tells Abram to leave country, kindred, and father's house for a land He will show, promising a great nation, blessing, and a name. Abram obeys at seventy-five, journeys through Canaan, and builds altars at Shechem and Bethel — the founding migration of Israel's history.
summary.zh: 神命亞伯蘭離本土親族父家，往所示之地，許以大國、祝福、大名。亞伯蘭七十五歲即行，經迦南，於示劍、伯特利築壇——以色列歷史之創始遷徙。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Now the LORD said unto Abram: 'Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto the land that I will show thee. And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and be thou a blessing.'

Abram went as the LORD had spoken, with Sarai and Lot and all their substance, into the land of Canaan, and passed through to Shechem, to the terebinth of Moreh. The LORD appeared and promised the land to his seed, and he built an altar; then he moved on to the hill country between Bethel and Ai, pitching his tent and calling on the name of the LORD. Paraphrase of Genesis 12:4-9 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Sarai in Pharaoh's Court

region.en: Egypt, Nile Delta (symbolic pin at Memphis)
region.zh: 埃及尼羅河三角洲（以孟斐斯象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Famine drives Abram to Egypt; fearing for his life he presents his beautiful wife as his sister, and Pharaoh takes her. Plagues strike Pharaoh's house until the truth is out; Abram is expelled rich — the first of the patriarchal 'sister-wife' episodes that read as foreshadowings of Israel's sojourns.
summary.zh: 饑荒驅亞伯蘭入埃及；恐失性命，以美妻為妹，法老遂取之。法老家遭災，真相大白；亞伯蘭攜財而出——族長「妻妹」敘事之首，預表以色列寄居諸章。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Say, I pray thee, thou art my sister; that it may be well with me for thy sake, and that my soul may live because of thee. And it came to pass, that, when Abram was come into Egypt, the Egyptians beheld the woman that she was very fair. The princes of Pharaoh also saw her, and praised her to Pharaoh; and the woman was taken into Pharaoh's house.
passages.note: Condensed verbatim from JPS 1917, Genesis 12:13-15 (public domain).

passages.text: For Sarai's sake the LORD plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues. Pharaoh summoned Abram: 'Why didst thou not tell me that she was thy wife?' and sent him away with his wife and all he had. The epos of Israel's later affliction in Egypt begins, ironically, with its first forefather protected there by plague. Paraphrase of Genesis 12:16-20 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Abram and Lot Divide the Land

region.zh: 伯特利，迦南山地

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Herds too large for one land force Abram and his nephew Lot apart. Generous Abram lets Lot choose; Lot picks the well-watered plain of the Jordan, settling near Sodom, while Abram dwells in Canaan and receives the promise of all the land he can see.
summary.zh: 牧畜眾多，地不能容，亞伯蘭與姪羅得分開。亞伯蘭寬宏任其先擇；羅得取約旦滋潤平原，近所多瑪而居；亞伯蘭居迦南，蒙應許舉目所見之地。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Abram said unto Lot: 'Let there be no strife, I pray thee, between me and thee, and between my herdmen and thy herdmen; for we are brethren. Is not the whole land before thee? separate thyself, I pray thee, from me: if thou wilt take the left hand, then I will go to the right; or if thou take the right hand, then I will go to the left.'

Lot lifted his eyes to the well-watered plain of the Jordan and journeyed east, pitching toward Sodom, whose men were wicked. After his departure the LORD told Abram to look north, south, east, and west: all the land he saw would be given him and his seed for ever, numerous as the dust of the earth. Paraphrase of Genesis 13:10-17 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The War of the Kings and Melchizedek's Bread and Wine
title.zh: 列王之戰與麥基洗德之餅酒

region.en: Valley of Siddim, Dead Sea (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 西訂谷，死海（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Four eastern kings raid the cities of the plain and carry off Lot; Abram musters 318 retainers, rescues him by night, and refuses all spoil. The mysterious priest-king of Salem, Melchizedek, blesses him with bread and wine — the Bible's first tithe scene and the seed of a whole royal-priestly tradition.
summary.zh: 四東方王掠平原諸城，擄走羅得；亞伯蘭率家丁三百一十八人夜襲救回，不受分毫戰利。撒冷王祭司麥基洗德以餅酒祝之——聖經首次什一奉獻，王祭合一傳統之源。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine: and he was priest of God the Most High. And he blessed him, and said: 'Blessed be Abram of God Most High, Maker of heaven and earth; and blessed be God Most High, who hath delivered thine enemies into thy hand.' And he gave him a tenth of all.

When Abram defeated the eastern coalition by a night march, the king of Sodom offered him the recovered goods; Abram swore by the LORD, God Most High, that he would not take so much as a sandal-thong, lest the king say 'I have made Abram rich' — save only the shares owed his allies and his men. Paraphrase of Genesis 14:21-24 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The Covenant Between the Pieces

region.zh: 幔利，希伯崙（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Childless Abram protests that his heir is a servant; God promises seed as the stars and, in a dread-smoking rite of cut animals passing between their halves, seals a covenant foretelling four hundred years of bondage and the deliverance to come — Abraham's first great vision.
summary.zh: 無子的亞伯蘭申訴繼者為僕；神應許後裔如眾星，並於烟與火爐中穿過剖開祭牲之間，立約預告四百年為奴與隨之拯救——亞伯拉罕首次大異象。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And He brought him forth abroad, and said: 'Look now toward heaven, and number the stars, if thou be able to number them'; and He said unto him: 'So shall thy seed be.' And he believed in the LORD; and He counted it to him for righteousness.

In a deep sleep a dread and great darkness fell on Abram, and God foretold: his seed would be a stranger in a land not theirs, afflicted four hundred years, 'but in the fourth generation they shall come back hither'. Then a smoking furnace and a flaming torch passed between the pieces of the sacrificed animals — God binding Himself alone while Abram slept. Paraphrase of Genesis 15:12-21 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Hagar at the Spring: The God Who Sees
title.zh: 夏甲在泉旁：看顧人的神

region.en: Wilderness of Shur, road to Egypt
region.zh: 書珥曠野，往埃及之路

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Sarai, barren, gives her Egyptian handmaid Hagar to Abram; when Hagar conceives, the two women's rivalry drives the pregnant girl into the wilderness. There an angel finds her by a spring, promises her a countless son, and she becomes the first person in scripture to give God a name: 'El Roi' — the God who sees.
summary.zh: 撒萊不育，以埃及使女夏甲予亞伯蘭；夏甲懷孕，二女相爭，孕者逃入曠野。天使於泉旁遇之，許其子不可勝數；她遂成聖經中首位為神命名者：「看顧人的神」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Hagar's story is also foundational in Islamic tradition (record cross-referenced there).

passages.text: And the angel of the LORD found her by a fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain in the way to Shur. And he said: 'Hagar, Sarai's handmaid, whence camest thou? and whither goest thou?' And she said: 'I flee from the face of my mistress Sarai.'

The angel promised that her seed would be multiplied beyond counting and named the boy Ishmael, 'God hears'. Hagar answered the first naming-theology in the Bible: 'Thou art a God that seest' — for she said, 'Have I even here seen Him that seeth me?' She returned and bore Abram a son in his eighty-sixth year. Paraphrase of Genesis 16:10-16 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Covenant of Circumcision: The Names Changed

region.zh: 幔利，希伯崙（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: God appears to ninety-nine-year-old Abram as El Shaddai, changes his name to Abraham ('father of a multitude') and Sarai's to Sarah, commands circumcision of every male as the covenant's sign 'throughout your generations', and promises the laughter-child Isaac within the year.
summary.zh: 神向九十九歲之亞伯蘭以全能神顯現，改名亞伯拉罕（萬族之父），撒萊改撒拉；命凡男丁割禮為約之記，「世世代代」，並許笑者以撒年內而生。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And I will establish My covenant between Me and thee and thy seed after thee throughout their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God unto thee and to thy seed after thee. ... This is My covenant, which ye shall keep, between Me and you and thy seed after thee: every male among you shall be circumcised.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 17:7, 10 (public domain); ellipsis marks omitted verses.

passages.text: Abraham fell on his face laughing at the news that a hundred-year-old man and ninety-year-old woman would bear a son, and asked that Ishmael 'might live before Thee'. God answered: the covenant would run through Isaac, born of Sarah, while Ishmael too would father twelve princes and a great nation. That very day Abraham circumcised himself, Ishmael, and every male of his house. Paraphrase of Genesis 17:17-27 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Three Visitors Under the Terebinths of Mamre

region.zh: 幔利，希伯崙（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Abraham runs from his tent to greet three men and serves them a feast; they repeat that Sarah will bear a son. Overhearing from the tent, ninety-year-old Sarah laughs — and God has the last word: 'Is anything too hard for the LORD?'
summary.zh: 亞伯拉罕奔出帳迎三客，設宴款待；三客重申撒拉將生子。撒拉在帳中暗笑——而神有末語：「耶和華豈有難成的事麼？」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. The narrative of hospitality (hachnasat orchim) became a foundational rabbinic paradigm of kindness.

passages.text: And the LORD appeared unto him in the plains of Mamre; and he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day; and he lifted up his eyes and looked, and, lo, three men stood over against him; and he saw, and ran to meet them from the tent door, and bowed down to the earth.

Abraham hurried Sarah to knead cakes, chose a calf, and set curds and milk before the men under the tree. 'Where is Sarah thy wife?' they asked, and repeated the promise. Sarah laughed within the tent, thinking of her worn body and her husband's age, and denied laughing — but the Visitor said: 'Nay; but thou didst laugh.' Paraphrase of Genesis 18:6-15 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Abraham Bargains for Sodom
title.zh: 亞伯拉罕為所多瑪講價

region.en: Overlook toward Sodom from Mamre (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 自幔利遙望所多瑪（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: God decides to tell Abraham what He plans for Sodom; Abraham stands before the LORD and haggles the city's minimum righteous population down from fifty to ten, asking: 'Shall not the Judge of all the earth do justly?' The boldest prayer-negotiation in scripture.
summary.zh: 神決意將所多瑪之謀告亞伯拉罕；亞伯拉罕立於耶和華前，將城中義人最低數自五十講至十，問曰：「審判全地的主，豈不行公義麼？」——聖經最大膽之祈禱講價。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Abraham drew near, and said: 'Wilt Thou indeed sweep away the righteous with the wicked? Peradventure there be fifty righteous within the city; wilt Thou indeed sweep away and not forgive the place for the fifty righteous that are therein? That be far from Thee to do after this manner, to slay the righteous with the wicked ... Shall not the Judge of all the earth do justly?'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 18:23-25 (public domain); ellipsis marks omitted verse.

passages.text: Step by step Abraham talked the LORD down: forty-five, forty, thirty, twenty — 'Oh, let not the LORD be angry, and I will speak yet but this once' — to ten. And the LORD went His way, and Abraham returned to his place. The dialogue models chutzpah in prayer: justice argued with the Judge Himself. Paraphrase of Genesis 18:26-33 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Lot at the Gate of Sodom

region.en: Sodom (traditional southern Dead Sea shore; symbolic pin)
region.zh: 所多瑪（傳統死海南岸；象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Two angels enter Sodom; Lot, like Abraham, runs to greet and feed them. The men of the city surround the house demanding the strangers; Lot offers his daughters instead; the angels strike the mob blind — the night that seals the city's doom.
summary.zh: 二天使入所多瑪；羅得如亞伯拉罕奔迎款待。城中之人圍屋索要客人；羅得竟以二女代之；天使使暴眾目盲——此夜城之厄運已定。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Later tradition read this as the paradigm of cruelty to strangers; the record states the narrative without endorsing later moralizations.

passages.text: And they called unto Lot, and said unto him: 'Where are the men that came in to thee this night? bring them out unto us, that we may know them.' And Lot went out unto them to the door, and shut the door behind him.

Lot pleaded with the crowd as 'brethren' and offered his two daughters, but the men of Sodom pressed upon him. The angels pulled Lot inside, shut the door, and smote everyone at the entrance with blindness, 'both small and great', so that they wearied themselves finding the door. Paraphrase of Genesis 19:8-11 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The Overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah

region.zh: 死海平原之南（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: At dawn the angels hurry Lot, his wife, and two daughters out of the doomed city — 'flee for thy life, look not behind thee'. Fire and brimstone rain from the LORD; Lot's wife disobeys, looks back, and becomes a pillar of salt, while Abraham sees the smoke of the plain rise like a furnace.
summary.zh: 黎明天使催促羅得夫婦與二女出城——「逃命吧，不可回顧」。耶和華降硫磺與火；羅得之妻違命回望，化為鹽柱；亞伯拉罕遠望平原烟氣上騰如燒窯。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And it came to pass, when they had brought them forth abroad, that he said: 'Escape for thy life; look not behind thee, neither stay thou in all the Plain; escape to the mountain, lest thou be swept away.' The sun rose as Lot entered Zoar, and the LORD rained upon Sodom and Gomorrah brimstone and fire out of heaven, overthrowing the cities and all the plain. Lot's wife looked back from behind him and became a pillar of salt. Abraham rose early that morning and looked down to see the smoke of the land going up as the smoke of a furnace — 'and God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow'. Paraphrase of Genesis 19:23-29 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 19:17 (public domain). / Paraphrase of Genesis 19:23-29 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Lot's Daughters in the Cave

region.zh: 瑣珥上方山地（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Fearing to dwell in Zoar, Lot retreats to a mountain cave. His daughters, believing the world's men are destroyed, make their father drunk on two successive nights to preserve their father's line; the sons born are Moab and Ben-ammi — the etiological, unflattering origin of Israel's neighbours the Moabites and Ammonites.
summary.zh: 羅得懼居瑣珥，退至山地洞中。二女以為世間男子盡滅，連續兩夜使父醉臥，以存父嗣；所生為摩押與便亞米——以色列鄰邦摩押亞捫之不榮起源釋義。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And the firstborn said unto the younger: 'Our father is old, and there is not a man in the earth to come in unto us after the manner of the whole earth. Come, let us make our father drink wine, and we will lie with him, that we may preserve seed of our father.'

Each daughter lay with her unknowing father on consecutive nights; both conceived. The elder bore a son named Moab — 'from the father' — ancestor of the Moabites; the younger bore Ben-ammi, father of the Ammonites. The Torah does not spare Israel's ancestors' kin: the nations' origins are told through shame. Paraphrase of Genesis 19:33-38 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Isaac Is Born: God Made Laughter

region.zh: 別是巴一帶，南地

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The LORD 'remembered Sarah as He had said' and the hundred-year-old promise is fulfilled: Sarah bears Abraham a son in his old age. They name him Isaac — 'laughter' — and Sarah's earlier cynical laugh becomes a public celebration: 'God hath made laughter for me; every one that heareth will laugh with me.'
summary.zh: 耶和華「照先前所說眷顧撒拉」，百年應許得成：撒拉於亞伯拉罕年老時生子，名以撒（笑）；昔日譏誚之笑化作慶賀：「神使我喜笑，凡聽見的必與我一同喜笑。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Sarah said: 'God hath made laughter for me; every one that heareth will laugh on account of me.' And she said: 'Who would have said unto Abraham, that Sarah should give children suck? for I have borne him a son in his old age.'

The LORD visited Sarah as He had promised; she conceived and bore Abraham a son at the set time God had spoken. Abraham named him Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day, being a hundred years old. Sarah weaned him, and Abraham made a great feast the day Isaac was weaned. Paraphrase of Genesis 21:1-8 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Hagar and Ishmael Sent Out into the Wilderness of Beersheba
title.zh: 夏甲與以實瑪利被逐於別是巴曠野

region.zh: 別是巴曠野，南地

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Sarah demands that Hagar's son be sent away 'for the son of this bondwoman shall not be heir'; God tells Abraham to listen to her. Hagar wanders until the water is spent, lays the dying boy under a bush, and weeps — until God opens her eyes to a well and promises the lad a great nation.
summary.zh: 撒拉求逐夏甲之子，「這使女的兒子不可與我的兒子以撒一同承受產業」；神命亞伯拉罕聽從。夏甲曠野漂流，水盡，將垂死之童置灌木下而泣——神開其目見井，並許此童成大國。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Ishmael's promise is foundational in Islamic tradition as well; cross-reference to islamic records planned.

passages.text: And God heard the voice of the lad; and the angel of God called to Hagar out of heaven, and said unto her: 'What aileth thee, Hagar? fear not; for God hath heard the voice of the lad where he is. Arise, lift up the lad, and hold him fast by thy hand; for I will make him a great nation.'

The matter grieved Abraham greatly, 'because of his son', but God confirmed Sarah's demand: 'in Isaac shall thy seed be called'. Hagar departed with bread and a skin of water into the wilderness of Beersheba; when the water was gone she cast the child under a shrub and sat opposite, weeping. Then God opened her eyes to a well; the lad grew in the wilderness, an archer, and took an Egyptian wife. Paraphrase of Genesis 21:11-21 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The Binding of Isaac (Akedah)

region.en: Mount Moriah, Jerusalem (traditional identification with the Temple Mount)
region.zh: 摩利亞山，耶路撒冷（傳統指聖殿山）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: God tests Abraham: 'Take now thy son, thine only son... and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there'. Father and son walk up the mountain in silence, the wood on Isaac's back; at the last moment an angel stays the knife, and a ram is offered instead. The Akedah is Judaism's supreme drama of faith and obedience.
summary.zh: 神試驗亞伯拉罕：「帶著你的兒子，就是你獨生的兒子……往摩利亞地去，在那裡把他獻為燔祭。」父子默然上山，柴在以撒背上；刀將落時，天使止之，遂獻公羊。阿刻達為猶太教信心順服之至高戲劇。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Central to Rosh Hashanah liturgy (shofar recalls the ram); treated as narrative, not as endorsement of child sacrifice, which the text itself replaces.

passages.text: And they came to the place which God had told him of; and Abraham built the altar there, and laid the wood in order, and bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar, upon the wood. And Abraham stretched forth his hand, and took the knife to slay his son.

Isaac had asked the only question on the road — 'the fire and the wood are here, but where is the lamb?' — and Abraham had answered, 'God will provide Himself the lamb'. As the knife rose, the angel of the LORD called twice: 'Lay not thy hand upon the lad, neither do thou any thing unto him; for now I know that thou fearest God'. Abraham looked up and saw a ram caught by its horns in a thicket, and sacrificed it instead. He named the place 'The LORD Will Provide', and the angel swore the great promise anew: 'thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies'. Paraphrase of Genesis 22:7-18 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Sarah Dies: The Purchase of Machpelah

region.zh: 希伯崙，麥比拉洞

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Sarah dies at Kiriat-arba (Hebron) at a hundred and twenty-seven. Abraham negotiates formally with the Hittites and buys the cave of Machpelah from Ephron for four hundred shekels of silver 'current money with the merchant' — the first land Abraham owns in the promised land, a grave.
summary.zh: 撒拉卒於基列亞巴（希伯崙），年一百二十七。亞伯拉罕與赫人正式議價，以四百舍客勒白銀「通用的銀子」購麥比拉洞——應許之地首業，乃一墳墓。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Machpelah (Tomb of the Patriarchs) remains a contested holy site today; record describes text only.

passages.text: And Abraham hearkened unto Ephron; and Abraham weighed to Ephron the silver, which he had named in the audience of the children of Heth, even four hundred shekels of silver, current money with the merchant. ... And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre — that is, Hebron — in the land of Canaan.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 23:16, 19 (public domain); ellipsis marks omitted verses.

passages.text: Abraham stood before the Hittites as 'a stranger and a settler' and asked for a burial site. Ephron, son of Zohar, publicly offered the cave 'in the presence of the people of the land', inflating the price; Abraham paid the full sum without haggling. The legal formality — witnesses, currency, field and cave with its trees — makes the patriarchs' tomb the first deeded property in Canaan. Paraphrase of Genesis 23:3-15 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: A Wife for Isaac: The Servant at the Well
title.zh: 為以撒娶妻：僕人在井旁

region.zh: 亞蘭拿哈蘭，哈蘭井旁

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Abraham sends his eldest servant to his kindred with ten camels, under oath never to take a Canaanite wife for Isaac. At the well the servant prays for a sign: the girl who waters him and his camels is the one. Rebecca's kindness to the camels proves her before a word is spoken.
summary.zh: 亞伯拉罕遣老僕攜十駝往本族，起誓勿為以撒娶迦南女。僕於井旁求兆：願為我與駝飲水者即是。利百加善待駝群，未出一言而自證。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And he said: 'O LORD, the God of my master Abraham, send me, I pray Thee, good speed this day, and show kindness unto my master Abraham. Behold, I stand by the fountain of water; and the daughters of the men of the city come out to draw water; and let it come to pass, that the damsel to whom I shall say: Let down thy pitcher, I pray thee, that I may drink; and if she say: Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also — let the same be she that Thou hast appointed for Thy servant, even for Isaac.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 24:12-14 (public domain); condensed without ellipsis.

passages.text: Before he finished speaking, Rebecca, born of Bethuel, came out with her pitcher, drew water for the stranger, and then ran again to the trough until all ten camels were satisfied. The servant gave her a nose-ring and bracelets and asked whose daughter she was; when she answered, he bowed his head and blessed the LORD who had led him 'in the right way'. Paraphrase of Genesis 24:15-27 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Rebecca Chooses: The Betrothal at Haran

region.zh: 哈蘭，彼土利之家

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The servant retells his mission in Laban's hall and asks for an answer; the family tries to delay, but Rebecca herself decides: 'I will go'. Meeting Isaac meditating in the field at evening, she alights from her camel, veils herself, and enters Sarah's tent — and Isaac is comforted after his mother's death.
summary.zh: 僕在拉班堂中覆述使命，求定奪；家人欲留，利百加自決：「我去」。以撒傍晚在田間默想，利百加下駝蒙面入撒拉之帳——以撒喪母之痛遂得安慰。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And they said: 'We will call the damsel, and inquire at her mouth.' And they called Rebecca, and said unto her: 'Wilt thou go with this man?' And she said: 'I will go.' The servant told of the signs at the well and laid out gifts; Laban and Bethuel answered that the matter was 'of the LORD' and could not be gainsaid. Morning gifts changed hands, the family blessed Rebecca to be 'mother of thousands of ten thousands', and she went. Isaac brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother, took her as wife, and loved her — and the text notes simply that Isaac was comforted for his mother. Paraphrase of Genesis 24:50-67 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 24:57-58 (public domain). / Paraphrase of Genesis 24:50-67 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Abraham's Later Sons and His Death at a Good Old Age
title.zh: 亞伯拉罕後嗣與其壽終

region.zh: 幔利，希伯崙（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: After Sarah's death Abraham takes Keturah, who bears six more sons — ancestors of the eastern tribes. He gives them gifts and sends them east, but gives all he has to Isaac; the sons of the concubines and Isaac himself bury him in Machpelah, where he is gathered to his people 'old and full of years'.
summary.zh: 撒拉卒後，亞伯拉罕娶基土拉，又生六子——東方諸族之祖。亞伯拉罕以財物遣之東去，卻將一切所有予以撒；眾子與以撒同葬之於麥比拉，「年老壽高」歸於本族。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Abraham gave all that he had unto Isaac. But unto the sons of the concubines, that Abraham had, Abraham gave gifts; and he sent them away from Isaac his son, while he yet lived, eastward, unto the east country.

Keturah's sons — Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, Shuah — would people the caravan routes of Arabia and the East, among them Midian, whose land would later shelter Moses. Abraham died at a hundred seventy-five and was buried by his two principal sons, Isaac and Ishmael, in the cave he had bought. Paraphrase of Genesis 25:1-10 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
